title: Instagram puts new limits on undisclosed AI profiles
content:
Instagram announced Monday that it’s changing how it labels AI-generated profiles and will start limiting the reach of accounts that feature AI-generated people without saying so.
The platform says it’s renaming its existing “AI creator” label to “AI-generated profile,” which Instagram says should make the disclosure easier to understand. The new label is meant to tell users that the person featured on a profile was generated or substantially created with AI.
Under the new policy, creators who don’t properly label an AI-generated profile could see their reach reduced. Creators who use the new label, on the other hand, won’t be penalized simply for having an AI-generated person as their profile subject.
The label also isn’t meant for every use of AI. Instagram says people who use AI to edit photos, polish captions, create graphics, or make other creative tweaks don’t need to use the AI-generated profile label.
Instagram says the change comes partly in response to users who have stumbled across profiles that looked like they belonged to real people, only to find out later that the person was completely AI-generated.
“As generative AI becomes a bigger part of how people create, we’ve heard that people don’t like seeing a profile that seems human, only to find out later that the person featured is AI-generated,” Instagram wrote. “They want to know when a profile features an AI-generated person.”
The timing is notable. Frustration over AI-generated content has been growing as AI influencers become more common across social media platforms.
For instance, earlier this year, the gay dating app Goose became the subject of a Wired investigation after a network of apparently AI-generated male influencers promoted the app on Instagram. Wired found more than two dozen accounts that appeared to feature AI influencers, some of which reportedly reached out to potential users through direct messages to get them to sign up.
Health and wellness content is another particularly worrying example. The New York Times reported in July it found hundreds of AI-generated doctors, healers, and wellness personalities on social media promoting supplements or making health claims to users.
The announcement comes after Instagram faced backlash over an AI tool that allowed users to generate images using other people’s likenesses. Users objected to having their public Instagram content used without an explicit opt-in. Meta then removed the feature.
Last week, Meta reached an $18 billion settlement with U.S. states over allegations concerning the effects of Facebook and Instagram on children and teenagers. As part of the agreement, Meta will introduce a default two-hour daily usage limit for teens across Facebook and Instagram, a “Night Mode” block, muted notifications during school hours, and other restrictions.

report.summary: Instagram renames AI creator label to 'AI-generated profile' and will limit reach of undisclosed AI-person profiles.
report.background: Meta's Instagram is tightening rules around AI-generated people. The change follows growing complaints from users who discover seemingly real profiles are fully AI. Recent scandals include a Wired investigation finding two dozen AI influencer accounts promoting the gay dating app Goose, and a New York Times report identifying hundreds of AI-generated doctors, healers, and wellness personalities making health claims on social media. Meta also faced backlash over a feature that generated images using people's likenesses without explicit opt-in, removing it. Around the same time, Meta reached an $18 billion settlement with U.S. states, agreeing to teen safety measures like a default two-hour daily usage limit. By renaming the label and penalizing non-disclosure, Instagram aims to balance AI creativity with transparency while responding to user demand for honest disclosure.
key_points: Instagram is renaming its 'AI creator' label to 'AI-generated profile' to make disclosure clearer. The new label explicitly tells users that the person featured was generated or substantially created with AI. It only applies when the profile's central subject is an AI-generated person, not for minor edits like retouching photos or polishing captions.

Undisclosed AI profiles will see reduced reach. Creators who fail to use the required label may see their content suppressed, while those who properly label their profiles won't be penalized just for featuring an AI-generated person. This creates a financial and visibility incentive to comply rather than hide AI involvement.

The policy responds to real-world abuses. Wired found a network of apparent AI male influencers promoting the dating app Goose, including direct messages encouraging sign-ups. The New York Times reported hundreds of AI-generated doctors and wellness influencers making health claims or promoting supplements. These cases show AI personas being used to deceive users for marketing and money.

The announcement arrives amid broader Meta scrutiny. The company removed an AI image feature that let users generate content using others' likenesses without opt-in. Meta also agreed to an $18 billion state settlement focused on teen safety, adding default daily limits and notification blocks. The AI profile label is part of a larger push to rebuild trust.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this signals platforms are moving from passive labeling to active algorithmic enforcement. Developers of AI personas and social media marketers must bake disclosure into their workflows or risk losing reach. For everyday users, clearer labeling helps prevent being misled by fake influencers pushing products, supplements, or health advice. For Meta, it is a trust-repair effort after several controversies. The real test will be enforcement: whether the system reliably catches undisclosed AI profiles and whether creators find loopholes by using 'substantially created with AI' definitions creatively. The policy could also set a precedent for other platforms considering similar rules.
report.tools: No specific open-source tools were referenced in the article. Developers and creators can watch Instagram's in-app AI disclosure settings and Meta's transparency features. Independent detection tools like Hive Moderation or Reality Defender can help identify AI-generated faces. For those building AI personas, following Instagram's label requirements is essential to avoid reach penalties.
